findings.title: Config-read failure modes for the new gate path are unspecified; fail-fast NFR not restated
findings.description: The gate introduces a new I/O path — `resolveGateConfig(config)` reads `workflow.review_*` from TOML on every status-derivation call — and names no failure handling for it. Verified against the code this design builds on: `ConfigManager.get()` rethrows non-ENOENT read/parse errors (malformed TOML in a hand-edited `.context-forge.toml` makes the call throw, and the design's data flow has no error branch), and `get()` performs no read-time validation (`validateValue` runs only in `set()`), so an out-of-enum `review_threshold` or non-boolean `review_enabled` can be returned raw. The design's stated narrowing ("`=== true` for `review_enabled`", Patterns and Conventions) then silently disables gating on a malformed value, and a value outside `ThresholdToken` reaches `evaluateVerdict` with no defined behavior — a silent fallback (against CLAUDE.md) and a "silent pass" the parent arch's **Fail-fast on configuration errors** principle forbids ("an invalid `workflow.review_threshold` value … surfaced immediately, not a silent pass or silent block"). That NFR is also not restated anywhere in the slice doc. Specify `resolveGateConfig`'s behavior for un-narrowable values (explicit error) and for a config-read throw, and restate the fail-fast requirement with its enforcement point.

findings.title: Arch requirement that the rationale name the parse failure explicitly is dropped
findings.description: 240-arch §Technical Considerations ("File-read failure modes") requires that for a review file that exists but cannot be parsed, "the rationale returned to the caller names the parse failure explicitly." The design instead embraces conflation — "a read failure and a missing frontmatter both surface as 'no verdict present'" — and TD-7's rationale contract names only review type, verdict, and threshold. Verified: `parseFrontmatter` returns the same `{ found: false, data: {} }` for a missing frontmatter block, an unclosed block, and any read/permission error, so the gate as designed cannot distinguish these cases and cannot name a parse failure. The failure-mode *handling* (→ `UNKNOWN` → `review_unknown_as`, never silently cleared) is correct; what is lost is the rationale-naming requirement. State how the unparseable case's rationale is worded (and record the deviation from the arch if "verdict absent or unparseable" is the accepted granularity), or capture the distinction.

findings.title: `STATUS` const does not cover the two new `SliceStatus` values this slice introduces
findings.description: TD-6 defines `STATUS` over the `NormalizedStatus` vocabulary (`complete`/`in-progress`/`not-started`/`deprecated`, union explicitly unchanged), but the slice's new statuses `pending-review`/`review-failed` live in the separate `SliceStatus.status` union (`introspection/types.ts:258`), and the design's own new code must assign and compare them (TD-3 routes `pending-review` → `review`, `review-failed` → `blocked`). Those values have no const entry, so the slice's own pattern — "No magic strings: … status values via `STATUS`; never a bare `'code'` or `'complete'` in the new code" — cannot be satisfied for exactly the values this slice adds, violating the project's define-once rule. Extend the const to cover the `SliceStatus` vocabulary (or add a second const), while keeping the `NormalizedStatus` derivation byte-identical for 910's sweep.
findings.location: project-documents/user/slices/241-slice.gate-logic-in-workflownavigator.md#TD-6: `STATUS` const introduced here; sweep deferred to 910

findings.title: `GateOutcome` includes `pending` but TD-2 assigns the pending outcome to the navigator
findings.description: TD-1 declares `evaluateVerdict(verdict, threshold, unknownAs): GateOutcome` with `GateOutcome = 'clears' | 'pending' | 'failed'`, but TD-2 states "the navigator supplies the `pending` outcome for the **absent** case from the `review === null` signal." Under that split `evaluateVerdict` can never return `pending` — the variant is dead or the ownership is contradictory. Clarify the return contract (drop `pending` from `evaluateVerdict`'s return, or route the absent case through it).

findings.title: Design resolves an arch-internal inconsistency in `pending-review` semantics
findings.description: 240-arch's slice-status extension allows "`pending-review` — … (or verdict is `UNKNOWN` and `review_unknown_as` treats it as pending)", yet the `review_unknown_as` enum (`fail`/`concerns`/`pass`) has no "pending" policy. The design's stricter resolution — present-but-unparseable is never `pending`, always `UNKNOWN` then policy — is consistent with the arch's own verdict-handling section and the "must not silently pass" principle, and is explicitly justified in TD-2. This is a correct resolution of a parent-document inconsistency; worth having 243 document the resolved semantics so the arch's parenthetical is not cited later.
